forms.negative: don't / doesn't + base verb

lessons.description: Simple = habit/fact. Continuous = live now.
lessons.usage: When: choose Simple vs Continuous. Cue: every/usually → Simple; right now / at the moment → Continuous.

lessons.title: B2 · Register

title: Past Simple
description: Finished deploys, incidents, and shipped changes with a clear past time.

lessons.title: A2 · Finished
lessons.description: Closed time. Cue: yesterday / last night / at 14:02.

forms.negative: didn't + base verb
forms.question: Did + subject + base verb?

title: Modals
description: Use can, could, should, must, and might for permission, advice, and risk in reviews and incidents.

lessons.title: A2 · Permission
lessons.description: can / should / must + base verb.
lessons.usage: When: ability, advice, or rule. Cue: can (able), should (advice), must (policy). Always + base.

forms.affirmative: can / could / should / must / might + base verb
forms.negative: can't / shouldn't / mustn't / might not + base verb
forms.question: Can / Should / Must / Might + subject + base verb?

exampleSentences: She must add tests to this patch.
This might be a race in the worker.
tips: Never should to / must to / can to. Never musts.
must not = prohibition; do not have to = not required.

lessons.title: B1 · Advice vs must
lessons.description: should = advice. must = policy. might = uncertain.
lessons.usage: When: pick the modal. Cue: policy/secret → must; review comment → should; hypothesis → might.

forms.affirmative: should / must / can / could / might + base verb
forms.negative: shouldn't / must not / couldn't / might not + base verb
forms.question: Could you + V? · Should we + V?

exampleSentences: You should extract the webhook handler.
Authors must not merge their own RFC.
Could you tail the worker logs?
We could not reproduce the timeout yesterday.
This spike might be a stale cache.
tips: Modal + base only (not can going, not should to).
must not is stronger than should not.

lessons.title: B2 · Register
lessons.description: RFC/review: must vs should vs might.
lessons.usage: When: written review. Cue: must for security; should for style; might for a guess.

forms.affirmative: Authors must + V · Reviewers should + V · This might + V
forms.negative: must not + V · should not + V · might not + V
forms.question: Must the RFC + V? · Should we + V?

exampleSentences: Authors must document the rollback for dual-write.
Reviewers should flag an unbounded retry.
The contract must reject unsigned tokens.
We should defer the Kafka cutover.
This patch might race the outbox worker.
tips: Do not hedge a hard policy with might.
could is past ability or polite option, not a security must.

lessons.title: C1 · Incident
lessons.description: War room: must (safety), might (hypothesis), should (next).
lessons.usage: When: incident English. Cue: we must page; it might be DNS; we should freeze deploys.

forms.affirmative: We must page · We should freeze · This might be replica lag
forms.negative: We must not fail over · This might not be the canary
forms.question: Must we page…? · Might this be…?

exampleSentences: We must page the primary for this SEV-1.
This might be replica lag, not a bad deploy.
We should silence the paging until triage ends.
I must not restart pods without a runbook step.
The RCA says we must treat p99 as a page.
tips: Hypothesis = might/could, not must, until you have evidence.
Keep modal + base under pressure.

title: Conditionals
description: Write zero and first conditionals plus unless for runbooks, flags, and paging rules.

lessons.title: A2 · If facts
lessons.description: Zero: If + present, present. unless = if not.
lessons.usage: When: a rule that is always true. Cue: If the job fails, it retries. No will in the if-clause.

forms.affirmative: If + present, present / imperative / will + V
forms.negative: If + present, do not + V · Unless + present, do not + V
forms.question: If + present, should we + V?

exampleSentences: If p99 exceeds 200ms, page the primary.

If the canary fails, rollback traffic.

tips: If-clause: present, not will. unless = if not.
First conditional (If + present, will) is for a real future.

lessons.title: B1 · If + will
lessons.description: Zero = always. First = real future. unless = if not.
lessons.usage: When: pick 0 vs 1. Cue: always/policy → If + present, present; tomorrow/risk → If + present, will.

forms.affirmative: If + present, will + V · If + present, present
forms.negative: Unless + present, will not + V · If + present, do not + V
forms.question: If + present, will we + V?

lessons.title: B2 · Policy

forms.negative: Unless + present, we do not + V · If + present, must not + V

lessons.title: B1 · Backshift
lessons.description: Reporting verb in the past → shift the inner tense.

title: Present Perfect Continuous
description: Talk about work that started earlier and is still running — investigations, syncs, reviews.

lessons.title: A2 · For / since
lessons.description: When an action started earlier and is still running. Cue: for / since / all morning.
lessons.usage: When: live work that started earlier and continues. Cue: for, since, all morning.

forms.negative: haven't/hasn't been + V-ing
forms.question: Have/Has + subject + been + V-ing?

exampleSentences: I have been investigating the 500s all morning.
She has been syncing the replica for an hour.
We have been reviewing the dual-write RFC since Monday.
QA has been testing the hotfix for two hours.
They have been paging the primary since 09:00.
tips: Do not use Present Perfect Continuous for a finished stamp (use Past Simple).
for + duration; since + start point.

lessons.title: B1 · Still running vs done
lessons.description: Pick Continuous Perfect vs Simple Perfect / Past when the hunt is open or closed.
lessons.usage: When: open hunt → have been + V-ing. Cue: still / so far / all day vs finished stamp.

forms.negative: have/has + PP (result now) vs Past (stamp)
forms.question: Have you been …? vs Have you … yet?

exampleSentences: We have been mitigating the leak since 14:02.
Have you finished the RCA yet?
I have been pairing on the flaky spec all sprint.

tips: Open activity → have been + V-ing. Finished result → have + PP or Past.
yet usually wants Present Perfect Simple, not Continuous.

lessons.title: B2 · Status updates
lessons.description: Write standup/Slack status with have been + V-ing without overclaiming a result.
lessons.usage: When: status that is still in flight. Cue: still / currently / all morning.

forms.negative: haven't been + V-ing
forms.question: Could you confirm how long … has been …?

Ask duration with how long + have/has been + V-ing.

lessons.title: C1 · War-room narrative
lessons.description: Separate the ongoing hunt from the timestamped move in one update.
lessons.usage: When: war-room voice. Cue: still investigating vs at 14:11 we shifted.

forms.negative: Do not put have been + V-ing next to at 14:02 as the key.

title: Verb Patterns
description: Choose to-infinitive vs gerund after need, avoid, keep, decide — common in Slack and PRs.

lessons.title: A2 · Need to / avoid -ing
lessons.description: After need/want use to + base. After avoid/keep use V-ing.
lessons.usage: When: choose to-infinitive vs gerund after common SE verbs. Cue: need to, avoid -ing.

forms.negative: not need to + base; avoid + V-ing
forms.question: Do we need to …? / Should we avoid …?

exampleSentences: We need to disable the flag before the deploy.
Please avoid merging during the freeze.
I want to pair on the flaky spec today.
QA decided to retest the hotfix tonight.
tips: need/want/decide → to + base. Never need to disabling.
avoid/keep/consider → V-ing. Never avoid to merge.

lessons.title: B1 · Pick the pattern
lessons.description: Choose to-infinitive vs gerund from the verb cue in Slack/PR.
lessons.usage: When: two real patterns compete. Cue: the verb before the blank.

forms.affirmative: verb cue picks to + base or V-ing
forms.negative: wrong pattern after the cue verb
forms.question: Should we avoid … or need to …?

exampleSentences: We need to page the primary for this SEV-1.
Authors agreed to keep dual-write for a sprint.
Please avoid restarting pods during the canary.
tips: suggest/avoid/keep/consider → V-ing.
need/want/decide/agree → to + base.

lessons.title: B2 · Review voice
lessons.description: Write polite review asks with the right pattern.
lessons.usage: When: PR/RFC comments. Cue: could you + base; avoid/consider + V-ing.

forms.negative: Do not write could you to merge.
forms.question: Could you …? / Would you mind …-ing?

exampleSentences: Could you extract the webhook handler?
Please consider adding an idempotency token.
Would you mind reviewing the dual-write RFC?
Authors should avoid storing raw secrets.
We need to document the rollback before ship.
tips: Polite ask: could you + base.
consider/mind/avoid → V-ing.

lessons.title: C1 · Incident decisions
lessons.description: Chain need to / avoid / keep during a SEV without broken patterns.
lessons.usage: When: war-room moves. Cue: we need to fail over; avoid flapping the canary.

forms.affirmative: need to + base; avoid + V-ing; keep + V-ing
forms.negative: No need to to / avoid to
forms.question: Do we need to … or keep …-ing?

exampleSentences: We need to shift EU traffic now.
Avoid flapping the canary on one spike.
Please keep tracing the 500s while we page.
On-call decided to fail over after forty minutes.
We agreed to freeze deploys until p99 recovers.
tips: Decision verbs (decide/agree/need) take to + base.
avoid/keep take V-ing even under SEV pressure.

title: Connectors
description: Link cause, result, contrast, and impact in Slack, PR, and incident updates.

lessons.title: A2 · Because / so
lessons.description: Link cause and result in one update. Cue: because (reason), so (result).
lessons.usage: When: join two workplace clauses. Cue: because / so.

forms.negative: Do not stack because so.
forms.question: Why…? → because …

exampleSentences: p99 spiked, so we rolled the canary.
I paired with QA because the spec was flaky.
Coverage dropped, so the pipeline blocked the deploy.
We disabled the flag because checkout returned 500s.
The replica lagged, so on-call paged the primary.
tips: because introduces the reason. so introduces the result.
One linker per join — do not write because so.

lessons.title: B1 · However / so / because
lessons.description: Pick the linker that matches contrast vs cause vs result.
lessons.usage: When: three linkers compete. Cue: contrast → however; reason → because; result → so.

forms.negative: Wrong linker for the logical relation
forms.question: Which linker fits the relation?

exampleSentences: The RFC is clear; however, dual-write still lacks a rollback.
CI is green, so we can merge after lunch.
We failed over because p99 burned the SLO.
Tests pass; however, the webhook contract changed.
I blocked the deploy because the canary flapped.
tips: however = contrast. because = reason. so = result.
Do not use however for pure cause.

lessons.title: B2 · Which means
lessons.description: Add a consequence clause after a metric or decision.
lessons.usage: When: explain impact. Cue: which means + clause.

forms.negative: Do not write which mean / that means without a clause
forms.question: What does this change mean for …?

exampleSentences: We keep dual-write one sprint, which means higher write load.
p99 is still red, which means we should freeze deploys.
Coverage dropped, which means the pipeline will block.
The token is required, which means unsigned JWTs fail.
EU traffic shifted, which means APAC stays on primary.
tips: which means + full clause (subject + verb).
Use it after a comma to spell the impact.

lessons.title: C1 · Incident narrative
lessons.description: Chain because / so / however / which means in a short RCA-style update.
lessons.usage: When: war-room or postmortem voice. Cue: mix linkers without doubling.

forms.negative: No because so / however because stacks
forms.question: Could you rewrite the timeline with clear linkers?

exampleSentences: p99 burned the SLO, so we shifted EU traffic.
We paged the primary because the replica lagged.
The canary looked healthy; however, checkout still returned 500s.
Dual-write stayed open, which means billing saw duplicates.
Please confirm the timeline uses because and so correctly.
tips: One clear relation per linker.
Ask for a rewrite when the RCA stacks because so.
